prize_parts.citation: For discoveries of the physiology of glucagon-like peptide-1 and of its biologically active form, which established the basis of incretin-based therapy for type 2 diabetes and obesity

statement.case_for: My preferred configuration is unchanged: a single prize part on B004 for Drucker, Holst and Mojsov. Round 1 did not shift my view of the science. It sharpened the one open question, which is the third name. Holst established GLP-1 secretion and its glucose-dependent insulinotropic action in humans, Drucker defined the proglucagon-derived peptide biology and receptor actions, and Mojsov identified and synthesised the biologically active truncated peptide that made the physiology tractable. That is original discovery work, and it is mature: the mechanism has been replicated for decades and the clinical consequence has been confirmed in large independent randomised trials for glycaemia, weight, and cardiovascular and renal outcomes. A citation confined to physiology and the active peptide keeps the prize in the discovery domain and lets the drugs stand as the demonstration that the mechanism is right. I do not rest this on the six-member alignment, which tells us nothing about whether the attribution is correct. The case holds because the chain from mechanism to medicine is unusually complete.
statement.case_against: Attribution is still the weak point, and the three-name limit means no B004 trio is complete. Habener is outside the credited names and several of us cite his group's proglucagon and GLP-1 peptide work as a possible priority claim against Mojsov, which I cannot resolve from the supplied record. The citation therefore names the active form of the peptide as a discovery and does not claim sole priority for it. Leaving out Knudsen is a real cost: liraglutide and semaglutide are the drugs patients take, and a physiology trio can be read as honouring the idea and not the delivery. I judge that cost smaller than displacing a discoverer, but it is a judgement and not a proof. A single-part prize also takes all three slots, so no second achievement can be added without cutting the GLP-1 trio. I do not regard that as a reason to add one.

responses.point: El-Manira keeps Drucker, Holst and Knudsen for B004 with a citation spanning physiology and drug development, and says he could accept Mojsov in place of Knudsen if the committee confines the citation to discovery. He also argues that imatinib should not be ranked so low.
responses.response: I take your Knudsen argument seriously: without durable acylated agonists the hormone would not have become a drug, and the outcome trials we cite depend on that step. But a span-to-development citation answers a different question from the one the Committee usually asks, which is who discovered the thing. You have said you would accept Mojsov if the citation is discovery-centred, and that is how I have worded mine, so our disagreement is narrower than the configurations suggest. I should also correct the record: my opening put optogenetics second, not third, as your response assumes. On imatinib I accept that its attribution is clean among the credited three and that it is mature. My reservation is the origin story. The Philadelphia chromosome and BCR-ABL work sit outside the credited trio, and the Lasker prize already recognised it. That keeps B007 a serious later candidate for me, not a rival to B004 this year.

responses.point: Perlmann proposes the same trio, keeps the prize on discovery, and notes that a popular choice such as B004 can crowd out candidates with a cleaner two-person story like the unfolded protein response (B032).
responses.response: I agree on the trio and on keeping the citation in the discovery domain. I also accept your crowding-out point as a real risk, since the committee should not default to the popular candidate. I have tested it, and B032 does not change my view. The attribution is clean and the discovery is original, but the direct disease consequences are still developing, which I said in round 1 and you said of your own second choice. If the committee wanted a pure-mechanism second part, Mori and Walter is the strongest one. That would cap the union at three people and force us to cut the GLP-1 trio to one name, which I think would damage the better-supported part. I am not willing to pay that price.

responses.point: Wahren-Herlenius ranks optogenetics (B043) second and calls it mature and overdue as a method. She also names the same B004 trio and says the priority for the bioactive peptide cannot be resolved from the record.
responses.response: We agree on B004, including that the Mojsov versus Habener question is not settled by anything we have. I have reread your overdue argument on B043 and I accept maturity. I still disagree on 'overdue', because the clinical translation is early and the credit is spread across Nagel, Hegemann, Bamberg, Boyden, Deisseroth and Miesenböck, with only three places. Any trio would be contestable, and a split prize with B004 would cost the incretin trio a name it needs. I keep B043 as an alternative because it is a major scientific achievement, not because I think a tool should outrank a mechanism-to-medicine discovery in the same year.

responses.point: Linnarsson moved from Knudsen to Mojsov after reading the attribution arguments and says the committee should test Mojsov's priority against the documentary record before the final ballot, not settle it by preference.
responses.response: I agree that this should not be settled by preference, and I would not want the committee to treat five matching trios as evidence that the question has been answered. What I can add is limited. The supplied record gives me Mojsov's identification and synthesis of the active GLP-1(7-36) peptide and Habener's proglucagon work, and it does not let me rank the two priority claims. Given that, I would carry the uncertainty into the citation wording by naming the biologically active form as a discovery without asserting first priority, and I would hold the Mojsov position as a judgement the committee should make explicitly, not as a default. I also note that you moved toward Mojsov, as I did, for reasons of credit and not of rank, and I do not think either of us has resolved the underlying question.

uncertainties: Whether Mojsov or Knudsen should hold the third B004 slot, and how much weight Habener's priority claim should carry given that the supplied record cannot resolve it.
Whether the citation should name only discovery or should span to drug development, which would change the credited trio.
Whether a second prize part would improve the configuration at all, given that it would cut the B004 trio to one name.
Whether B018 can be credited fairly without Eshhar, and whether B043 can be allocated among six claimants.
statement.conflict_note: No candidate-specific conflict is apparent from my profile. I have documented co-authorship of about twenty works with committee colleague Thomas Perlmann and a postdoctoral link to Paul Greengard, but neither involves a credited name on the shortlist. As chair I am responsible for the process, which does not constitute a conflict. My neurology background is noted and is not treated as a conflict. The disclosures by El-Manira, Sandberg, Wahren-Herlenius and Linnarsson in round 1 do not change my assessment.
